channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Trump China trip: Iran and Ukraine not in 'peace declaration' and more takeaways
item.description: Trump heads back to Washington after meeting with Xi and Putin -- the first sitdown between the three superpowers -- with no tangible diplomatic breakthroughs in hand.

item.title: Fiona the hippo dies at Cincinnati Zoo after swallowing hat
item.description: The beloved hippo died after swallowing a hat that accidentally fell into her habitat last week, the zoo said Thursday.

item.title: 'We're seeing in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity', expert says
item.description: FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Dr. R. David Edelman, Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution, also former Director for Cybersecurity on the National Security Council under the Obama administration. He explains that the latest spate of network outages shows "in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity" adding that "the one thing that's tying most of these outages together is that companies and institutions are racing to patch a system that's been identified as vulnerable, and they're patching what themselves are pretty creaky digital systems".

item.title: Kushner says Trump 'open' to extend NATO mutual defense-type clause to Ukraine
item.description: US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday that President Donald Trump was open to extending to Ukraine a security guarantee similar to NATO's mutual defense clause, but stressed that Washington has to protect its interests too. The comments came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz qualified the summit between the presidents of the United States, Russia and China as a "photo op". FRANCE 24's international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert explains.

item.title: Macron urges Ukraine's allies to 'reopen the question' of NATO membership
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday called for Ukraine's allies to speed up the delivery of urgently needed air defence systems and urged them to "reopen the question" of Ukraine's NATO membership after talks in Berlin aimed at reaffirming European support for Kyiv.

item.title: Ambulance service declares 'critical incident'
item.description: London Ambulance Service said it has declared a "critical incident" in response to sustained high demand, with more than 7,000 calls a day over three consecutive days.

item.title: Trump’s CISA pick rejects Jan. 6 as an 'attack,' won't name 2020 election winner
item.description: Michael LoSapio, President Donald Trump's nominee to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, says he doesn't consider the Jan_ 6 Capitol insurrection an "attack."

item.title: A president among body bags: Photo ops spark outrage in Colombia
item.description: Since taking office in August, Colombia's far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella has regularly posted videos that show him walking among body bags supposedly holding the remains of rebel fighters – a communications strategy that has sparked widespread criticism.

item.title: Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
item.description: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.

item.title: Three of a kind? Xi hosts Trump and Putin as Ukraine war grinds on
item.description: Gang of three or glorified photo op? Xi Jinping hosting Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Already, our Monday panel rejected attempts to paint the three-way meeting as a new Yalta, as in the 1945 sit-down on the Black Sea that defined the post-war security architecture of Europe.

item.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting: Trump's recognition of China and Russia as 'peers of the US'
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Olivia Cheung. The trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit was significant despite the absence of concrete agreements, according to Cheung. “The significance is seen in the precedence of the United States seeing and giving recognition that China and Russia are peers of the United States,” she explained, adding that “the image of a G3 is very significant.”

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 phones home from record one light-day away, 49 years after launch
item.description: The Voyager 1 probe launched by NASA nearly a half century ago has reached a distance from Earth of one light day (more than 26 billion kilometres), the farthest any human artifact has ever ventured from our planet. The space agency received a signal from the spacecraft Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent.

item.title: WATCH: Our colleague skips work to play GTA 6
item.description: ABC News associate producer Ben Greenberg took a vacation day to play “Grand Theft Auto VI” and told Kyra Phillips about it live.

item.title: What Obama said to newly elected Democrats after midterm gains
item.description: Former President Barack Obama told Democratic U.S. House members-elect on Wednesday that they should value their ideological diversity even if they have disagreements.

item.title: Auditors concerned about billions ICE is spending to expand immigration detention
item.description: Federal auditors warn that ICE is spending billions of dollars to expand immigration detention without "determining the cost effectiveness" of new initiatives.

item.title: WATCH: Trump calls Putin, Xi his friends after meeting
item.description: Doug Lute, former U.S. ambassador to NATO, says President Donald Trump referring to Putin and Xi as friends is "concerning for America's allies."

item.title: The 'Magic Six': How to strengthen your marriage in midlife
item.description: How do we maintain healthy romantic relationships as we age? Allison Aubrey and Scott Detrow talk about about the science of healthy, later-in-life relationships.

item.title: French media regulator says it will monitor top YouTubers for bias in election coverage
item.description: Rules designed to safeguard media pluralism during elections campaigns will apply to France's most influential YouTubers in the run-up to next year's presidential contest, media regulator Arcom warned on Thursday, reflecting the growing influence of content creators whose audiences often outstrip those of traditional media companies.

item.title: WATCH: 'Kenan and Kel' star has a mission to give back
item.description: Actor Kel Mitchell shares how he's using his star power to help families in need.

item.title: What impact will the Shenzhen summit have on the US-China trade war?
item.description: Despite warm words between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen Thursday, the simmering trade war between Washington and Beijing still looks to be no closer to resolution.

item.title: Bangladesh: Hasina supporters vandalise ruling party office
item.description: Hundreds of supporters of ousted Bangladesh premier Sheikh Hasina staged street protests on Thursday, as a wave of arson attacks escalated tensions ahead of her planned return from exile next month.

item.title: Susan Smith denied parole again 32 years after drowning sons in a South Carolina lake
item.description: Susan Smith, convicted of killing her two sons by rolling her car into a South Carolina lake in 1994, was denied parole again

item.title: US has 'unbalanced approach' on DR Congo deal, Rwanda's foreign minister says
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe said the Trump administration had "an unbalanced approach" in implementing the DR Congo peace deal it brokered. He also said that the recent row over the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie's top job was "manufactured in Paris and Kinshasa". Finally, he defended a deal for Rwanda to host failed asylum seekers from five European countries.

item.title: How much do businesses want to pay for AI?
item.description: Four years after ChatGPT went mainstream, generative AI is transforming how we live and work. It's also been a major driver of economic growth, with massive amounts of money poured into expanding global computing capacity. But now, there are signs of a slowdown in AI spending as companies take a reality check: are they getting sufficient returns on their investments and how much artificial intelligence do they actually need?

item.title: Inside France's mental health crisis: Are the French all right?
item.description: This week, we try to get inside the heads of French people, with a deep dive into mental health in France. For a nation that loves analysing its problems, its mental health figures make for sobering reading: nearly one in five French people are affected by a mental health issue.

item.title: ICJ ruling on Myanmar genocide: ‘Historic victory for Rohingya, landmark for international justice’
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Reed Brody, Member of the International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Lawyer and veteran war crimes prosecutor. The International Court of Justice's ruling on Myanmar marks, according to Brody, "a historic victory for the Rohingya, but also a landmark for international justice." He explains how the court assessed evidence of genocidal intent, rejecting Myanmar's justification of its military operations as counterterrorism. He argues that "the existence of an armed conflict or a security objective doesn't exclude genocidal intent," a finding he believes will have "far-reaching implications in future genocide cases," including South Africa's case against Israel over Gaza. Brody also discusses the Gambia's role in bringing the case and growing challenges to international accountability, warning that "we're in a very dangerous moment."

item.title: Xi demonstrating China's 'global status', occupying 'central position' in relation to Trump & Putin
item.description: Sharon Gaffney is pleased to welcome Rex Li, professor of international relations at King's College London. For Professor Li, the meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in China is less about "reaching concrete agreements and a common position." Rather, he argues, it is about demonstrating Xi's ability to bring the American and Russian leaders together to discuss major geopolitical issues. Li believes that Xi Jinping has the most to gain from the meeting, as it allows him to demonstrate China's global status and its role as a diplomatic convener. Putin may also benefit from the opportunity to meet the two leaders despite Russia's international isolation following its invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: EU reveals it suffered 'AI-powered' cyber attack
item.description: The EU has revealed it suffered a cyber attack powered by AI last month and some of its digital tools are still offline as a result.

item.title: Gender pay gap: French women work "for free” from today
item.description: Women in Europe are still paid less than men, with the gap falling from 15.1% in 2016 to 11.1% in 2024, according to Eurostat. In France, women symbolically start working for free from 10:51 am on Thursday, 19 November, and at the current pace equality would not be reached until 2062. Experts warn that AI could make things worse by eliminating administrative and legal jobs where many women work, while childbirth and short paternity leave continue to slow women’s careers.

item.title: 'GTA VI': A masterpiece? Fans react to gaming's biggest release
item.description: Critics are calling the new "Grand Theft Auto VI" a masterpiece. In this edition of arts24, we hear what fans make of one of the biggest video game releases in history. We also look at U2's new album and tour marking 50 years of the band, discover the French comic book that Pope Leo is reading and meet the women redefining Mexico's Mariachi tradition.

item.title: The chocolate countdown: The art of the advent calendar
item.description: The holiday season is almost upon us and with it come advent calendars. The annual physical countdown originated in 19th-century Germany as a Christian tradition to count down the days until Christmas. Eugénie Pont from the magazine Fou de Pâtisserie tells us more about what we can expect from the biggest chocolate makers in France.

item.title: Trump, Xi, Putin summit: What was it all about?
item.description: Donald Trump has left China after a historic first meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Ukraine was discussed without Kyiv or European leaders in the room, which raised eyebrows, though Trump defended dialogue with rivals and Putin said the talks created conditions for future agreements. Xi warned major powers against conflict, and topics included reducing nuclear risks, reforming the UN and increasing energy flows.

item.title: WATCH: Military family gets surprise of a lifetime at 2026 CMAs
item.description: "GMA" sponsor Chevrolet teams up with rising country star Zach Top to surprise a military family.

item.title: Behind the UK's use of AI in asylum applications
item.description: The UK is increasingly turning to artificial intelligence to manage its immigration system, from analysing migrants’ phones to processing asylum applications. But what happens when AI gets involved in deciding how an asylum seeker's story is understood? Stella Elgersma, journalist at InfoMigrants, explains how the UK Home Office is testing AI tools to process asylum applications, including a system that generates summaries of asylum interviews. With errors, limited human oversight and concerns over transparency, could AI put asylum seekers’ lives at risk?

item.title: Haiti: Salvador’s Bukele publishes video of attack on gang leader’s house
item.description: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said Wednesday that his troops demolished the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti known as Jeff Gwo Lwa. "My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières," Bukele wrote on X - referencing a 1803 battle critical in helping secure Haiti's independence from France.

item.title: Beaujolais Nouveau: A French tradition uncorked
item.description: Every year on the third Thursday of November, France raises a glass to one of its most joyful traditions: Le Beaujolais Nouveau! That means that this Thursday, millions of bottles of the 2026 young red wine will be uncorked around the world, from Lyon to New York. Olivier Badoureaux, wine expert and director of the French trade organisation Inter Beaujolais, tells us what we should expect from this year's vintage.

item.title: France: Retirees march against 2027 budget cuts
item.description: More than a thousand people marched in Paris on Thursday, called by a union alliance joined by student and high-school groups, to protest social and tax measures targeting retirees in the 2027 budgets. The government wants retirees to contribute about €5.4 billion, by freezing the indexation of pensions above €1,260 and reforming their 10% income tax allowance. Union leaders say the money should not come from retirees’ pockets, as FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago explains.

item.title: WATCH: NASA's Voyager 1 now a light-day away after 1977 launch
item.description: NASA launched its Voyager 1 space probe in 1977. It's made it more than 16 billion miles in space, marking the farthest any human made object has ever traveled.

item.title: Burnham says Europe 'ready to enter negotiations' to help end Russia's war in Ukraine
item.description: Europe is ready to enter negotiations to help end Russia's war in Ukraine, Andy Burnham has said.

item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman in Oregon who helped reunite a missing cat with its owner in South Carolina.

item.title: The U.N.'s top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during military operations in the northern Rakhine state in 2017.

item.title: World Toilet Day is a funny idea with a serious goal: A world awash in toilets
item.description: Yahoo for the loo! November 19 marks the 25th anniversary of World Toilet Day. The theme this year: "Sanitation and Gender Equality: Safe Toilets, Equal Futures."
